scene: Once upon a time there was a poor husbandman who had many children and little to give them in the way either of food or clothing. They were all pretty, but the prettiest of all was the youngest daughter, who was so beautiful that there were no bounds to her beauty.
caption: [A poor husbandman had many children, but the youngest daughter was so beautiful there were no bounds to her beauty]

scene: It was late on a Thursday evening in autumn, and wild weather outside, terribly dark, and raining so heavily and blowing so hard that the walls of the cottage shook. They were all sitting together by the fireside when suddenly some one rapped three times against the window-pane.
caption: [It was a wild Thursday evening, terribly dark, with rain and wind so hard the cottage walls shook]

scene: The man went out to see what could be the matter, and when he got out there stood a great big white bear. The white bear greeted him and asked if he would give him his youngest daughter—if he would, they should be as rich as they were now poor.
caption: "Will you give me your youngest daughter? If you will, you shall be as rich as you are now poor."

scene: The man thought he must first ask his daughter about this. He went in and told them that there was a great white bear outside who had faithfully promised to make them all rich if he might but have the youngest daughter.
caption: [The man went in and told them about the white bear who promised to make them rich]

scene: The youngest daughter said no, and would not hear of it. The man went out again and settled with the White Bear that he should come again next Thursday evening and get her answer.
caption: "She said no, and would not hear of it."

scene: The man persuaded his daughter, talking so much to her about the wealth they would have and what a good thing it would be for herself, that at last she made up her mind to go. She washed and mended all her rags and made herself as smart as she could.
caption: [The father persuaded her, and at last she made up her mind to go]

scene: Next Thursday evening the White Bear came to fetch her. She seated herself on his back with her bundle, and thus they departed. When they had gone a great part of the way, the White Bear asked if she was afraid.
caption: "Are you afraid?"

scene: "No, that I am not," said she. The White Bear told her to keep tight hold of his fur, and there was no danger. And thus she rode far, far away, until they came to a great mountain.
caption: "Keep tight hold of my fur, and then there is no danger."

scene: The White Bear knocked on the mountain, and a door opened, and they went into a castle where there were many brilliantly lighted rooms which shone with gold and silver. There was a large hall with a well-spread table, so magnificent it would be hard to make anyone understand how splendid it was.
caption: [They entered a castle with brilliantly lighted rooms shining with gold and silver]

scene: The White Bear gave her a silver bell and told her that when she needed anything she had but to ring this bell, and what she wanted would appear.
caption: "When she needed anything she had but to ring this bell, and what she wanted would appear."

scene: After she had eaten, night was drawing near and she grew sleepy after her journey. She rang the bell, and scarcely had she touched it before she found herself in a chamber where a bed stood ready made for her, as pretty as anyone could wish to sleep in.
caption: [She rang the bell and found herself in a chamber with a bed as pretty as anyone could wish]

scene: It had pillows of silk, and curtains of silk fringed with gold, and everything that was in the room was of gold or silver. But when she had lain down and put out the light a man came and lay down beside her.
caption: [The room had pillows of silk and curtains fringed with gold, and everything was of gold or silver]

scene: Behold it was the White Bear, who cast off the form of a beast during the night. She never saw him, however, for he always came after she had put out her light, and went away before daylight appeared.
caption: [The White Bear cast off the form of a beast during the night, but she never saw him]

scene: So all went well and happily for a time, but then she began to be very sad and sorrowful, for all day long she had to go about alone. She did so wish to go home to her father and mother and brothers and sisters.
caption: [She began to be very sad and sorrowful, for all day long she had to go about alone]

scene: The White Bear asked what it was that she wanted. She told him it was so dull there in the mountain, and that she had to go about all alone, and that in her parents' house there were all her brothers and sisters.
caption: "It is so dull there in the mountain, and I have to go about all alone."

scene: The White Bear said there might be a cure for that, if she would but promise him never to talk with her mother alone, but only when the others were there too. Her mother would take hold of her hand and want to lead her into a room alone.
caption: "Never talk with your mother alone, but only when the others are there too."

scene: One Sunday the White Bear said they could now set out to see her father and mother. She sat on his back and they journeyed a long, long way until they came to a large white farmhouse. Her brothers and sisters were running about outside playing.
caption: [They came to a large white farmhouse where her brothers and sisters were playing outside]

scene: The White Bear told her that her parents dwelled here now, but she must not forget what he had said, or she would do much harm both to herself and to him. She said she would never forget.
caption: "Do not forget what I said to you, or you will do much harm both to yourself and me."

scene: There were such rejoicings when she went in to her parents that it seemed as if they would never come to an end. Now they had everything that they wanted, and everything was as good as it could be.
caption: [There were such rejoicings when she went in that it seemed as if they would never come to an end]

scene: In the afternoon, after they had dined, all happened just as the White Bear had said. Her mother wanted to talk with her alone in her own chamber.
caption: [Her mother wanted to talk with her alone in her own chamber]

scene: She remembered what the White Bear had said, and would on no account go. "What we have to say can be said at any time," she answered. But somehow or other her mother at last persuaded her.
caption: "What we have to say can be said at any time."

scene: She was forced to tell the whole story. She told how every night a man came and lay down beside her when the lights were all put out, and how she never saw him, because he always went away before it grew light.
caption: [She told how every night a man came and lay down beside her when the lights were put out]

scene: "Oh!" cried the mother, in horror, "you are very likely sleeping with a troll! But I will teach you a way to see him. You shall have a bit of one of my candles, which you can take away with you hidden in your breast."
caption: "You are very likely sleeping with a troll! But I will teach you a way to see him."

scene: The mother warned her to look at him with the candle when he was asleep, but take care not to let any tallow drop upon him. So she took the candle and hid it in her breast.
caption: "Look at him with that when he is asleep, but take care not to let any tallow drop upon him."

scene: When evening drew near the White Bear came to fetch her away. On their way he asked if everything had not happened just as he had foretold, and she could not but own that it had.
caption: "If you have done what your mother wished, you have brought great misery on both of us."

scene: When she had reached home and had gone to bed it was just the same as it had been before. A man came and lay down beside her, and late at night, when she could hear that he was sleeping, she got up and kindled a light.
caption: [Late at night, when she could hear he was sleeping, she got up and kindled a light]

scene: She lit her candle, let her light shine on him, and saw him. He was the handsomest prince that eyes had ever beheld, and she loved him so much that it seemed to her that she must die if she did not kiss him that very moment.
caption: [He was the handsomest prince that eyes had ever beheld, and she loved him so much]

scene: So she did kiss him; but while she was doing it she let three drops of hot tallow fall upon his shirt, and he awoke.
caption: [She kissed him, but let three drops of hot tallow fall upon his shirt, and he awoke]

scene: "What have you done now?" said he. "You have brought misery on both of us. If you had but held out for the space of one year I should have been free."
caption: "What have you done now? You have brought misery on both of us."

scene: He told her that his step-mother had bewitched him so that he was a white bear by day and a man by night. But now all was at an end between them, and he must leave her and go to her. She lived in a castle which lay east of the sun and west of the moon.
caption: "I have a step-mother who has bewitched me. I must leave you and go to her castle east of the sun and west of the moon."

scene: "There too is a princess with a nose which is three ells long, and she now is the one whom I must marry." She wept and lamented, but all in vain, for go he must.
caption: "There too is a princess with a nose which is three ells long, and she now is the one whom I must marry."

scene: She asked him if she could not go with him. But no, that could not be. She asked if he could tell her the way, and she would seek him.
caption: "Can you tell me the way then, and I will seek you?"

scene: "Yes, you may do that," said he; "but there is no way thither. It lies east of the sun and west of the moon, and never would you find your way there."
caption: "It lies east of the sun and west of the moon, and never would you find your way there."

scene: When she awoke in the morning both the Prince and the castle were gone, and she was lying on a small green patch in the midst of a dark, thick wood. By her side lay the self-same bundle of rags which she had brought with her from her own home.
caption: [When she awoke both the Prince and the castle were gone, and she lay in a dark, thick wood]

scene: She rubbed the sleep out of her eyes and wept till she was weary. Then she set out on her way, and walked for many and many a long day, until at last she came to a great mountain.
caption: [She wept till she was weary, then set out and walked for many and many a long day]

scene: Outside the mountain an aged woman was sitting, playing with a golden apple. The girl asked if she knew the way to the Prince who lived east of the sun and west of the moon, and who was to marry a princess with a nose three ells long.
caption: "Do you know the way to the Prince who lives east of the sun and west of the moon?"

scene: The old woman asked how she happened to know about him. "Maybe you are she who ought to have had him." "Yes, indeed, I am," said she. The old woman said she knew nothing about him but that he dwelt in a castle east of the sun and west of the moon.
caption: "Maybe you are she who ought to have had him."

scene: The old woman said she would be a long time in getting to it, if ever she got there at all. But she would lend her her horse, and she could ride on it to an old woman who was a neighbor of hers.
caption: "You shall have the loan of my horse, and then you can ride to an old woman who is a neighbor of mine."

scene: She gave the girl the golden apple, and told her when she had got there to just strike the horse beneath the left ear and bid it go home again.
caption: "When you have got there you must just strike the horse beneath the left ear and bid it go home again."

scene: The girl seated herself on the horse and rode for a long, long way. At last she came to the mountain where an aged woman was sitting outside with a gold carding-comb.
caption: [She rode for a long, long way, until she came to a mountain with an aged woman and a gold carding-comb]

scene: The girl asked if she knew the way to the castle east of the sun and west of the moon. The old woman said what the first old woman had said: she knew nothing about it but that it was east of the sun and west of the moon.
caption: "I know nothing about it, but that it is east of the sun and west of the moon."

scene: The old woman gave her the loan of her horse to the nearest old woman who lived next, perhaps she might know. And she gave her the gold carding-comb, for it might perhaps be of use to her.
caption: "You shall have the loan of my horse to the nearest old woman. Take the gold carding-comb—it may be of use."

scene: The girl seated herself on the horse and rode a wearisome long way onward. After a very long time she came to a great mountain where an aged woman was sitting spinning at a golden spinning-wheel.
caption: [She rode a wearisome long way and came to a mountain with an aged woman spinning at a golden wheel]

scene: The girl asked this old woman too if she knew the way to the Prince. "Maybe it was you who should have had the Prince." "Yes, indeed, I should have been the one," said the girl.
caption: "Maybe it was you who should have had the Prince."

scene: This old crone knew the way no better than the others—it was east of the sun and west of the moon, she knew that, and the girl would be a long time in getting to it. But she might have the loan of her horse, and she had better ride to the East Wind.
caption: "You had better ride to the East Wind. Perhaps he may know where the castle is, and will blow you thither."

scene: The old woman gave her the golden spinning-wheel, saying perhaps she might find she had a use for it. When she got to the East Wind she must just strike the horse beneath the left ear and he would come home again.
caption: "Perhaps you may find that you have a use for it."

scene: The girl had to ride for a great many days before she got there. At last she arrived and asked the East Wind if he could tell her the way to the Prince who dwelt east of the sun and west of the moon.
caption: "Can you tell me the way to the Prince who dwells east of the sun and west of the moon?"

scene: The East Wind said he had heard tell of the Prince and of his castle, but he did not know the way to it, for he had never blown so far. But if she liked he would go with her to his brother the West Wind: he might know that, for he was much stronger. She might sit on his back, and he would carry her there.
caption: "I do not know the way, but if you like I will go with you to my brother the West Wind."

scene: She seated herself on the East Wind's back, and they went so swiftly. When they got there, the East Wind went in and said the girl was the one who ought to have had the Prince up at the castle east of the sun and west of the moon.
caption: [The East Wind carried her swiftly to the West Wind]

scene: The West Wind said so far he had never blown so far as that. But if she liked he would go with her to the South Wind, for he was much stronger, and he had roamed far and wide, and perhaps he could tell her what she wanted to know.
caption: "I have never blown so far. But I will go with you to the South Wind."

scene: She journeyed to the South Wind, and the West Wind asked him if he could tell her the way to the castle that lay east of the sun and west of the moon, for she was the girl who ought to marry the Prince who lived there.
caption: [The West Wind carried her to the South Wind]

scene: "Oh, indeed!" said the South Wind, "is that she?" He said he had wandered about a great deal in his time and in all kinds of places, but he had never blown so far as that. If she liked, however, he would go with her to the North Wind, for he was the oldest and strongest of all.
caption: "I have never blown so far as that. But I will go with you to the North Wind."

scene: She sat on the South Wind's back and they went in great haste. When they came near the North Wind's dwelling, he was so wild and frantic that they felt cold gusts a long while before they got there. "What do you want?" he roared out from afar, and they froze as they heard.
caption: "What do you want?" he roared out from afar, and they froze as they heard.

scene: The South Wind told him it was he, and this was she who should have had the Prince who lived in the castle east of the sun and west of the moon. She wished to ask if he had ever been there and could tell her the way.
caption: [The South Wind told the North Wind she was looking for the Prince]

scene: "Yes," said the North Wind, "I know where it is. I once blew an aspen leaf there, but I was so tired that for many days afterward I was not able to blow at all."
caption: "Yes, I know where it is. I once blew an aspen leaf there."

scene: The North Wind said if she was really anxious to go there, and was not afraid to go with him, he would take her on his back and try if he could blow her there. "Get there I must," said she, "and I have no fear, no matter how fast you go."
caption: "Get there I must, and I have no fear, no matter how fast you go."

scene: The North Wind said she must sleep there to-night, for if they were ever to get there they must have the day before them.
caption: "You must sleep here to-night, for we must have the day before us."

scene: The North Wind woke her betimes next morning and puffed himself up, and made himself so big and so strong that it was frightful to see him. Away they went, high up through the air.
caption: [He woke her betimes next morning and made himself so big it was frightful to see]

scene: They went high up through the air as if they would not stop until they had reached the very end of the world. Down below there was such a storm! It blew down woods and houses, and when they were above the sea the ships were wrecked by hundreds.
caption: [It blew down woods and houses, and when they were above the sea the ships were wrecked by hundreds]

scene: They tore on and on, and a long time went by, and still they were above the sea. The North Wind grew tired, and more tired, and at last so utterly weary that he was scarcely able to blow any longer.
caption: [The North Wind grew tired and more tired, and at last so utterly weary he could scarcely blow]

scene: He sank and sank, lower and lower, until at last he went so low that the waves dashed against the heels of the poor girl he was carrying. "Art thou afraid?" said the North Wind. "I have no fear," said she.
caption: "Art thou afraid?" "I have no fear."

scene: There was just enough strength left in the North Wind to enable him to throw her on to the shore, immediately under the windows of a castle which lay east of the sun and west of the moon. But then he was so weary and worn out that he was forced to rest for several days.
caption: [He threw her on the shore under the windows of the castle east of the sun and west of the moon]

scene: Next morning she sat down beneath the walls of the castle to play with the golden apple. The first person she saw was the maiden with the long nose, who was to have the Prince.
caption: [She sat beneath the walls playing with the golden apple, and saw the maiden with the long nose]

scene: The long-nosed princess opened the window and asked how much she wanted for that gold apple. The girl answered it could not be bought either for gold or money.
caption: "How much do you want for that gold apple of yours, girl?"

scene: The Princess asked what would buy it. The girl said if she could go to the Prince who was here and be with him to-night, the princess should have the golden apple. The Princess said she might do that.
caption: "If I may go to the Prince and be with him to-night, you shall have it."

scene: So the Princess got the golden apple. But when the girl went up to the Prince's apartment that night, he was asleep, for the Princess had so contrived it.
caption: [The Princess got the golden apple, but when the girl went up that night the Prince was asleep]

scene: The poor girl called to him and shook him, and between whiles she wept; but she could not wake him. In the morning as soon as day dawned, in came the Princess with the long nose and drove her out again.
caption: [She called to him and shook him and wept, but she could not wake him]

scene: In the daytime she sat down once more beneath the windows of the castle and began to card with her golden carding-comb. The Princess asked her what she wanted for it. She said it was not for sale, but if she could get leave to go to the Prince and be with him during the night, she should have it.
caption: [She sat beneath the windows carding with her golden carding-comb]

scene: When she went up to the Prince's room he was again asleep. Let her call him, or shake him, or weep as she would, he still slept on, and she could not put any life in him.
caption: [He still slept on, and she could not put any life in him]

scene: When daylight came in the morning, the Princess with the long nose came too, and once more drove her away.
caption: [In the morning the Princess with the long nose drove her away again]

scene: When day had quite come, the girl seated herself under the castle windows to spin with her golden spinning-wheel. The Princess with the long nose wanted to have that also.
caption: [She sat under the castle windows spinning with her golden spinning-wheel]

scene: The Princess opened the window and asked what she would take for it. The girl said what she had said on each of the former occasions—that it was not for sale, but if she could get leave to go to the Prince and be with him during the night, she should have it.
caption: "If I can go to the Prince and be with him during the night, you shall have it."

scene: "Yes," said the Princess, "I will gladly consent to that."
caption: "Yes, I will gladly consent to that."

scene: In that place there were some Christian folk who had been carried off. They had been sitting in the chamber next to the Prince, and had heard how a woman had been in there who had wept and called on him two nights running. They told the Prince of this.
caption: [Christian prisoners heard a woman weeping and calling on the Prince two nights running]

scene: That evening when the Princess came once more with her sleeping-drink, the Prince pretended to drink, but threw it away behind him, for he suspected it was a sleeping-drink.
caption: [The Prince pretended to drink the sleeping-drink but threw it away behind him]

scene: When the girl went into the Prince's room this time he was awake, and she had to tell him how she had come there. "You have come just in time," said the Prince, "for I should have been married to-morrow."
caption: "You have come just in time, for I should have been married to-morrow."

scene: He said he would not have the long-nosed Princess, and she alone could save him. He would say he wanted to see what his bride could do, and bid her wash the shirt which had the three drops of tallow on it.
caption: "I will say I want to see what my bride can do, and bid her wash the shirt with the three drops of tallow."

scene: The Princess would consent to do it, for she did not know it was the girl who had let the tallow fall on it. But no one could wash them out but one born of Christian folk: it could not be done by one of a pack of trolls.
caption: "No one can wash them out but one born of Christian folk: it cannot be done by one of a pack of trolls."

scene: Then he would say no one should ever be his bride but the woman who could do this, and he knew that she could. There was great joy and gladness between them all that night.
caption: [There was great joy and gladness between them all that night]

scene: The next day, when the wedding was to take place, the Prince said, "I must see what my bride can do." "That you may do," said the stepmother.
caption: "I must see what my bride can do." "That you may do."

scene: He had a fine shirt which he wanted to wear as his wedding shirt, but three drops of tallow had got upon it which he wanted to have washed off. He had vowed to marry no one but the woman who was able to do it.
caption: "I have a fine shirt with three drops of tallow. I have vowed to marry no one but the woman who can wash them out."

scene: That was a very small matter, they thought, and agreed to do it. The Princess with the long nose began to wash as well as she could, but the more she washed and rubbed, the larger the spots grew.
caption: [The Princess began to wash, but the more she washed, the larger the spots grew]

scene: "Ah! you can't wash at all," said the old troll-hag, who was her mother. "Give it to me." But she too had not had the shirt very long in her hands before it looked worse still, and the more she washed it and rubbed it, the larger and blacker grew the spots.
caption: "Give it to me." But the more she washed, the larger and blacker grew the spots.

scene: The other trolls had to come and wash, but the more they did, the blacker and uglier grew the shirt, until at length it was as black as if it had been up the chimney.
caption: [The trolls washed, but the shirt grew blacker and uglier until it was as black as if it had been up the chimney]

scene: "Oh," cried the Prince, "not one of you is good for anything at all! There is a beggar-girl sitting outside the window, and I'll be bound that she can wash better than any of you! Come in, you girl there!"
caption: "Not one of you is good for anything at all! Come in, you girl there!"

scene: So she came in. "Can you wash this shirt clean?" he cried. "Oh! I don't know," she said; "but I will try."
caption: "Can you wash this shirt clean?" "I will try."

scene: No sooner had she taken the shirt and dipped it in the water than it was white as driven snow, and even whiter than that. "I will marry you," said the Prince.
caption: [She dipped the shirt in the water and it was white as driven snow]

scene: Then the old troll-hag flew into such a rage that she burst, and the Princess with the long nose and all the little trolls must have burst too, for they have never been heard of since.
caption: [The old troll-hag flew into a rage and burst, and all the trolls burst too]

scene: The Prince and his bride set free all the Christian folk who were imprisoned there, and took away with them all the gold and silver that they could carry.
caption: [They set free all the Christian folk and took away all the gold and silver they could carry]

scene: They moved far away from the castle which lay east of the sun and west of the moon.
caption: [They moved far away from the castle east of the sun and west of the moon]
